name: get_calendar_events
description: this tool gets all calendar events for a specified period.
arguments_prompt:
Arguments to this tool are the start time string and end time string

start_date: str (required)
end_date: str (required)
calendar_names: list (optional)
single_events: bool (optional, default False)
event_name_contains: str (optional) — case-insensitive substring filter against event title. Use this when the user asks for a specific event by name (e.g. 'Friday Night Meats', 'dentist appointment') rather than a general scan. Keep the date range wide enough to contain occurrences, and let this filter narrow the result to the named event in one call.

**DEFAULT RANGE: Use 1 week (7 days) unless the user specifically asks for a different time period.** If using event_name_contains for a named recurring event whose next occurrence may be days away, widen to 2-4 weeks.

Today is {{ date }}.

**Examples:**
- For "check my calendar": Use today to 7 days from now
- For "what's on my calendar this week": Use today to end of this week
- For "any meetings tomorrow": Use tomorrow's start/end
- For "calendar for next month": Use start/end of next month
- For "find the Friday Night Meats event" / "what's the Zoom link for X": Use today to 4 weeks out, set event_name_contains="friday night meats" (or the distinctive part of the name)

[WARNING] Avoid ambiguity at midnight: Times exactly at 00:00:00 can be misinterpreted as either the start or end of a day. When setting boundaries, explicitly choose 23:59:59 (end of the previous day) or 00:01:00 (start of the new day) for clarity.

Time zone will be automatically set so don't worry about that we are looking for simple ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) dates.

calendar_names is a list subset of: [primary, Birthdays, Food, Work]. Omit this to search all calendars.

**single_events parameter (IMPORTANT):**
- `single_events=True` (RECOMMENDED): Returns actual event instances with specific start/end times. Use this for queries about specific dates like "today", "tomorrow", "this week".
- `single_events=False`: Returns recurring event "masters" (rule definitions like "Occurs weekly on Friday") without calculating specific instances. Only use this if you specifically need the recurrence rules.

For most calendar queries, use `single_events=True` to get usable event times.
